newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil rate moves seen not too hard on 97 inflation.
newsitem.headline: Brazil rate moves seen not too hard on 97 inflation.

text.p: Brazilian government estimates that increases in telephone and electricity rates, which will weigh on inflation indices between April and July, will not have too significant an impact on annual inflation, a local newspaper said.

Gazeta Mercantil said the Finance Ministry expects the rate increases to have an impact of one percentage point on the Fipe consumer price index, 0.34 percentage points on the IGP-DI index and 0.48 percentage points on the National Consumer Price Index (INPC).
The Finance Ministry said those increases would not affect projections of lower inflation in 1997, according to the newspaper.
In 1996 Brazil posted an annual inflation rate of just above 10 percent, the lowest level since the 1950s.

The telephone rate restructuring will represent an increase of 8.3 percent on average on subscribers' telephone bills and will allow for a 3.1 percent net increase in revenues for telecommunications operators, it said.
The average 9.92 percent increase in electricity rates will have an impact of 0.04 percentage points in April and 0.32 percentage points in May on the Fipe index.
The IGP-DI index will rise by 0.02 percentage points in April, while the INPC index will rise by 0.10 percentage points. the newspaper added.
